transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 16:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Arielle Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Lena Patel (Nimbus Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Nimbus SRE), Olivia Gomez (Nimbus Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Goal: Signoff on pilot acceptance thresholds and reporting format; agree scope and timeline for benchmark run.
- Agreed workload profiles, go/no-go thresholds, and reporting artifact. Next run window scheduled.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timeline, routing/policy, security (KMS/VPC)

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Arielle Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Arielle, AE on the Redwood side, Diego is our SE. Is this time still good for everybody?
[00:06] Lena Patel: Yeah, thanks, Arielle. Good to see you both. We wanted to get this signoff so we can run the pilot next week.
[00:10] Diego Martinez: Great. We'll run through the acceptance checklist, the three workload profiles you sent, and the reporting artifact. We'll capture any outstanding items.
[00:18] Olivia Gomez: Quick ask up front — we need the reporting to be automatable, CSV or JSON, we can't have manual slide decks.
[00:23] Arielle Chen: Absolutely, we'll provide both CSV and a canonical JSON schema. We'll show an example at the end.
[00:29] Marcus Lee: Also want to confirm network/security — we want VPC peered tests and use our KMS for any keys in on-prem mode.
[00:35] Diego Martinez: Yep, we can run the Dedicated mode against a reserved test pool and for Private we can accept a KMS key ARN. We'll need the peering CIDR and firewall rules — we'll capture that as an action item.

[00:45] Lena Patel: On the success criteria — our internal bar is twofold: latency and quality. For latency we care about p95 for the real-time inference route, for quality we have a labeled set of 500 verification prompts.
[00:55] Arielle Chen: Can you confirm the three workload profiles again for the record?
[00:58] Olivia Gomez: Sure — Profile A: real-time chat inference, sequence lengths typically 1–256 tokens, 60 reqs/s target during peak; Profile B: embeddings/batch 512-length slices, 200 qps burst but processed as 100 rps steady; Profile C: reranking/beam-like with long context ~2–4k tokens, lower qps (5–10 rps) but heavy memory.
[01:18] Diego Martinez: Good separation. For the pilot we'll emulate all three. Our recommended test: run each profile for 30–60 minutes to stabilize caches and measure steady-state.
[01:28] Marcus Lee: Do you plan to use KV/prefix caching during the runs? We use a lot of repeated prompts.
[01:32] Diego Martinez: Yes. We'll have two modes: cold-cache and warm-cache. Warm-cache run will simulate prefix hits using your provided trace. That matters a lot for cost and p95.

[01:40] Lena Patel: Okay, thresholds. We're proposing: Profile A p95 latency < 250 ms and 99th < 450 ms, Profile B embedding throughput >= 100 rps with median latency < 80 ms, Profile C end-to-end rerank p95 < 1.2s and accuracy on the verification set > 92%. Does that align with Redwood expectations?
[02:02] Arielle Chen: Those are reasonable. From Redwood side we suggest making one conservative pass: p95 < 300 ms for A, but we can commit to 250 ms if we configure batching and dedicate capacity. For C we want the accuracy gate to be > 90% at minimum; 92% is fine if you validate labeling.
[02:20] Diego Martinez: Also important — token accounting. We'll provide per-route per-second token rates and cost projection. For example, Profile A average tokens per response ~60 tokens, that helps size the dedicated pool.

[02:30] Olivia Gomez: How will you report model variance? We have concerns about hallucinations on the long-context reranker.
[02:34] Diego Martinez: We'll run the labeled 500 prompt set and produce per-example scores: correctness flag, model output, and normalized hallucination metrics. We'll include a brief qualitative sample of 20 fails.

[02:45] Lena Patel: Reporting format callout — we need a single-line CSV per inference event with columns: timestamp, route, request_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, model_name, kernel_variant, cache_hit_boolean, correctness_flag. Also we want an aggregate JSON with p50/p95/p99 and throughput per route.
[03:05] Arielle Chen: Confirmed. We'll provide the CSV spec and a sample JSON summary. We'll include kernel_variant because you might see differences between quantized and fp16 runs.

[03:12] Marcus Lee: On security/compliance — we asked about audit logs retention and SOC2. Do you have a short note?
[03:17] Arielle Chen: Yes, Redwood provides audit logs for every request in Dedicated and Private modes. We have SOC2 Type II and can share the attestation doc. For Private you'll manage the control plane and keys; for Dedicated we store minimal telemetry and you can request a longer retention window as an add-on. We'll attach the security pack.

[03:33] Olivia Gomez: Network — for the Private run we'll need guidance on firewall rules. Marcus will send the CIDR.
[03:38] Marcus Lee: I'll send peering details and the KMS key ARN. One ask: can Redwood run the benchmark inside our VPC and write logs to our S3 bucket?
[03:46] Diego Martinez: Yes, we support S3 sink via STS role and can write CSV reports directly to your bucket during the run. We'll need the role ARN and a bucket policy.

[03:55] Lena Patel: Back to acceptance gates — we want go/no-go rules spelled out. Can we do a pass/fail matrix?
[04:00] Arielle Chen: Sure. Proposed go/no-go:
- Go if all three profiles meet primary latency/throughput thresholds AND accuracy gate for Profile C >= 92% on labeled set.
- Conditional go if two profiles pass and one is marginal (within 10%) and there's an agreed remediation plan (e.g., increase dedicated GPUs, change quantization).
- No-go if any profile fails by more than 20% or accuracy < 88% or there are critical stability issues (error rate > 1%).

[04:27] Diego Martinez: We'll also provide per-minute time series so you can see degradation during bursts. If the error rate spikes during cache warm-up we'll annotate that.

[04:36] Marcus Lee: For margins, do you include network tail latency? Our infra team measures 95th network latency of 60–80ms between our VPC and Redwood test endpoint — that'll be in the noise.
[04:44] Diego Martinez: We'll instrument both sides: agent-side latency and server-side compute latency. Report will split network vs compute so we can apportion blame.

[04:53] Olivia Gomez: Who signs the acceptance after the run? We need an explicit approval process so procurement can close the PO.
[04:58] Arielle Chen: We propose a short acceptance doc that lists metrics and a signoff block for Nimbus (Lena + Marcus) and Redwood (Arielle). After the run, the acceptance doc will be filled automatically using the report metrics and emailed to the stakeholders for e-signature.

[05:12] Lena Patel: Timeline sanity check — we want the run this week so the PO can go through finance by end of month. Is your team available to run 12/22–12/24?
[05:19] Diego Martinez: Yes, we can run within that window. We'll need your traffic trace and KMS/CIDR by 12/21.

[05:25] Marcus Lee: One more technical: quantization profiles. We might want to test int8 quantized variant vs fp16 for cost delta. Can you highlight where kernel_variant will reflect that?
[05:33] Diego Martinez: Kernel_variant will be "fp16", "int8-qtz", or internal label like "q5_kvopt". We'll include cost per token for each variant and an expected throughput curve.

[05:42] Olivia Gomez: For the reranker verification, we want the sample of failed cases to include both the input and the top-3 model outputs, plus a short annotator note.
[05:50] Arielle Chen: We'll include that. We'll also include simple charts of precision/recall and confusion for the labeled set.

[05:58] Lena Patel: Ok I think we can sign off if the CSV schema and run window are provided. Real quick — any blockers from Redwood infra?
[06:05] Diego Martinez: No major blockers. We will want to reserve a small dedicated pool for the Profile A high qps tests to avoid noisy neighbors. That requires a short provisioning step but we can do that quickly.

[06:14] Arielle Chen: So to recap — agreed items: share harness + sample report (Arielle), Nimbus to share traffic trace and prompts (Lena), run window 12/22–12/24, reporting artifacts CSV + JSON summary, go/no-go matrix as discussed. We'll capture action items in the notes.

[06:27] Olivia Gomez: Looks good. Also please include a quick appendix in the report describing how caching was simulated and the exact seed for trace replay.
[06:33] Diego Martinez: Will do. We'll include the run script and the exact seeds to ensure reproducibility.

[06:38] Marcus Lee: I'll send the VPC and KMS details right after this meeting.

[06:41] Arielle Chen: Great. Final question from my side — any legal or procurement asks to surface now?
[06:46] Lena Patel: Just the usual — we will need the SOC2 and the standard EULA redlines. Procurement will review after trial results.

[06:50] Arielle Chen: Great, we'll attach SOC2 and security pack to the shared folder tonight.

[06:55] Olivia Gomez: Thanks, everyone.
[06:57] Arielle Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the harness link and the CSV spec by EOD tomorrow.

--- End transcript ---

Meeting wrap / short recap (auto):
- Pilot acceptance gate set: go if all three profiles hit the thresholds, conditional go if single profile within 10% margin plus remediation plan, no-go if >20% failure or accuracy <88% or error rate >1%.
- Reporting: per-event CSV and aggregate JSON with p50/p95/p99, throughput and cost estimates.
- Timeline: benchmark run scheduled 2026-12-22 to 2026-12-24; follow-up review 2026-12-28.
